title: Check, edit, check again in one turn stays refused: the ordinary fail, fix, rerun cycle needs a further turn
outcome: A worker whose check fails, who fixes the code, commits and reruns in the same turn earns evidence for the last clean check, without a further turn, and a real edit after that check is still refused. Not a prerequisite for the first evaluation window; required before any permanent enforcement.
acceptance: A deterministic test against a pinned real Engram, on the product without w-776305458d13: one turn with a registered check A at X, an edit and commit to Y, and a clean registered check B at Y, then close and evaluate, is shown refused
After the fix that same sequence earns evidence for check B with no further turn, on Linux and on Windows, and Engram is unchanged
A real edit after check B is still refused, and an edit reverted to earlier content is not accepted as unchanged unless the measured content really matches
No wait is added to a turn or a send, and no new assertion depends on real time
disposal_reason: Superseded by the simple rule Greg approved („tak”, 2026-11-04 about 20:19Z, memory rules-greg-eo-one-check-2026-11-04): Engram's w-633b5cacc42a decides from Git and carries the real-host rows, so these settled-baseline rows aren't needed. Branches and evidence kept; see note 05115e96.
